memos.headline: S04 at 52-week high with RSI 75; S02 in freefall at -51.5% drawdown; S10 surging with best 4-week relative strength
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation across the universe today. S04 is sitting exactly at its 52-week high with RSI 75 and +12.9% above its 50-day mean — a strong trend but stretched enough that I'd wait for a pullback to the 50d before adding. S10 has the most explosive momentum with +20.7% over 4 weeks and +14.7% relative strength vs SPY over the same period, though at nearly 20% above its 50d mean a mean-reversion risk is real; I'd stay long but tighten stops below ~130. S02 is a catastrophe: -51.5% from its high, -41.2% below the 200d mean, RSI 33.9, and still bleeding with -21.4% over 4 weeks — there is no sign of a bottom and I would not touch it until it reclaims at least its 50d average. S08 and S09 are both below their 200d means with negative 12-week relative strength, classic laggards I'd avoid until they prove otherwise.

views.note: At 52-week high with persistent relative strength (+15.5% vs SPY over 12w), but RSI 75 and +12.9% above 50d mean warrant caution; a close below 440 would change my view.
Best 4-week momentum in the universe at +20.7% with strong relative strength, but +19.7% above 50d mean is extremely stretched; would reassess below 130.
Steady uptrend with +16.6% over 12 weeks, only -5.1% from high, RSI 61, and +10.5% above 200d — the cleanest trend with lowest volatility (ATR 1.56%); a break below 250 would concern me.
Recovering well with +11.2% over 4 weeks and +5.2% relative strength vs SPY, RSI 66 is healthy; still -11.8% from high so needs to clear ~242 to confirm breakout.
Down -51.5% from high, -41.2% below 200d mean, RSI 33.9 with no stabilization visible — classic falling knife; would reconsider only on a sustained move above 380.
Sitting right at its 50d mean but -9.4% below 200d with -13.2% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks; needs to reclaim 220 to show life.
Below both moving averages with -7.7% 4-week relative strength and -11.7% 12-week relative strength vs SPY; would need a close above 110 to reconsider.
Flat at its 50d mean with RSI 48 and low volatility (ATR 1.44%), but -9.8% 12-week relative strength vs SPY keeps me sidelined; a move above 170 could shift this.
Decent 4-week bounce of +12.6% but still -15.8% from high and -3.3% 12-week relative strength vs SPY; needs to clear 185 to confirm trend change.
Good 4-week bounce of +9.0% but still -15.2% from high and below 200d mean; reclaiming 360 with follow-through would turn me constructive.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Lead on Margin Expansion; S07 and S09 Show Earnings Compression
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable, high-margin growers and names where earnings power is deteriorating. S10 stands out with 69.2% YoY revenue growth, a 42.6% net margin, and only $8.46B in total debt — the cleanest balance sheet in the group. S05 delivered a 38.3% net margin on $90.23B of revenue with net income up 46.0% YoY, while S04 posted a 36.9% margin with 17.7% net income growth, both showing operating leverage I want to own. On the other end, S07's revenue fell 9.8% YoY with net income down 29.8% on a $31.74B debt load, and S09 is essentially flat on revenue with a 6.2% decline in net income — both signal cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for. I would revisit S07 if revenue stabilizes and margins stop contracting, and I would revisit S09 if net income growth turns positive.

views.note: 69.2% YoY revenue growth, 42.6% net margin, and minimal debt of $8.46B make this the strongest fundamental profile in the universe.
38.3% net margin with 46.0% YoY net income growth on $90.23B revenue and only $14.79B debt reflects exceptional earnings power.
36.9% net margin, 13.3% revenue growth, and 17.7% net income growth on manageable $42.88B debt show durable profitability.
64.2% YoY net income growth on $155.67B revenue is impressive, though the 11.0% net margin and $58.75B debt leave less room for error.
26.0% net margin is solid but revenue growth of only 5.1% and $92.20B in total debt suggest limited upside from here.
32.3% net margin is attractive but $407.22B in total debt dwarfs the rest of the universe and net income grew only 9.1% YoY.
19.1% net margin is decent but revenue declined 2.1% YoY and net income was essentially flat at +0.4%.
9.8% revenue growth is respectable but a 5.7% net margin and $81.27B debt with unavailable YoY net income comparison limit conviction.
Flat revenue (+0.1% YoY), declining net income (-6.2%), and a thin 9.3% margin signal earnings compression I don't want to own.
Revenue down 9.8% and net income down 29.8% YoY with $31.74B in debt is a clear deterioration in earnings power.

memos.headline: Fed Pausing at 4.50% With Rising Unemployment and Steepening Curve Favors Duration-Sensitive Growth Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 4.50% for three months, while the effective rate sits at 4.33%. CPI is running at +2.3% YoY—benign enough to keep cuts on the table but not urgent enough to force action. The labor market is softening, with unemployment at 4.2%, up 30bp over the past year and 20bp over just three months, signaling a mild slowdown. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+91bp YoY to +0.48pp) and the 10y yield has risen 22bp over three months to 4.51%, suggesting the market is pricing in term premium and eventual easing rather than imminent recession. A surprise jump in CPI above 3% or unemployment breaching 4.5% would change my regime call from 'pause/mild slowdown' to either 'hiking risk' or 'recession risk,' respectively.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from a pause-to-easing trajectory with contained inflation at 2.3% YoY.
Steepening curve (+91bp YoY in 10y-2y spread) supports bank net interest margins in a pause regime.
Staples offer defensive positioning as unemployment drifts higher, but limited upside if slowdown stays mild.
Cyclicals face headwinds from rising unemployment (+20bp in 3m) and a mild slowdown regime.
Energy lacks a clear macro catalyst; stable rates and modest slowdown leave the sector range-bound.
Growth-oriented names should benefit as the market prices eventual easing with 10y yields near cycle highs.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S04 and S10 Positive Momentum vs. S02 and S08 Negative Overhang
memos.body: I see a clear split in the universe based on earnings-driven sentiment and subsequent filing activity. S04 posted a +7.6% reaction to its Apr-30 results and S10 gained +3.2% on its May-28 print, both suggesting positive narrative momentum that may not yet be fully crowded. On the negative side, S02's -22.4% earnings-day collapse on Apr-17 was followed by three separate director departure/appointment filings through Jun-4, signaling ongoing management instability that keeps sentiment toxic. S08 dropped -3.7% on its May-1 results and has been quiet since a single Other Events filing on May-12, offering no catalyst for tone recovery. S01 fell -3.7% on Q3 earnings but is actively presenting at Deutsche Bank as of Jun-5, which could mark an inflection—I'm watching but not yet convinced the narrative has turned.

views.note: Strongest positive earnings reaction in the universe at +7.6%; no subsequent negative filings suggest the upbeat tone persists.
Fresh +3.2% earnings beat on May-28 is the most recent positive catalyst in the set and sentiment should still be building.
A -22.4% earnings shock followed by four director change filings in seven weeks signals deep management turmoil and persistently negative sentiment.
Negative -3.7% earnings reaction with no positive follow-up filing; tone remains depressed with no visible recovery catalyst.
Earnings-day +4.0% pop and steady Reg FD disclosures suggest constructive management engagement, though the move is six weeks old and may be priced.
Negative -3.7% Q3 reaction but active investor outreach via Deutsche Bank presentation on Jun-5 hints at a possible tone inflection—too early to call.
Mild +1.7% earnings reaction and high filing volume (four 8-Ks in three weeks) suggest stable but unremarkable sentiment.
Flat +0.4% earnings reaction and routine shareholder vote filing offer no directional sentiment signal.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Easing but Still Elevated; Geopolitical Risk Backdrop Favors Defensive Positioning
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 340.80 remains historically elevated despite a 12.9% decline over three months, while the VIX at 18.48 has dropped sharply (-21.8% 1m), suggesting markets are pricing in calmer waters faster than the policy environment warrants. HY OAS at 3.18% tightened 42bp over the past month but is still 30bp wider than three months ago, indicating credit markets retain some caution about the macro backdrop. WTI at $64.06 is up 9.5% month-over-month but down 3.8% over three months, consistent with supply-side OPEC+ management rather than a demand-driven rally—this limits upside for energy-exposed names from a geopolitical premium standpoint. Without specific detail in the 8-K filings beyond item codes, I have limited visibility into company-level geopolitical exposure, so my conviction is moderate; an escalation in export controls or new sanctions would shift me more defensively across the board.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in three weeks suggest active corporate developments, but without content detail I cannot assess geopolitical exposure; staying neutral until clarity emerges.
Multiple Reg FD disclosures suggest proactive investor communication amid elevated policy uncertainty, but no clear geopolitical catalyst to take a directional view.
Fresh Reg FD filing on June 5 and steady disclosure cadence suggest management is front-footing communication; declining VIX and tightening HY spreads provide a supportive risk backdrop.

Only a single mid-April 8-K with no follow-up filings; in an environment where policy uncertainty remains at 340.80, the lack of disclosure raises concern about unaddressed geopolitical or regulatory risk.
Single 8-K in May with no detail on geopolitical exposure; WTI's mixed signals and still-elevated policy uncertainty keep me sidelined.
Two filings in April-May suggest routine disclosure; no evidence of geopolitical headwinds or tailwinds specific to this name.
